name: Hapa Build-versus-Integrate Guide
status: decision framework; not a pricing sheet or performance forecast
reusableFoundations: explicit human approval and bounded authority

integrateWhen: a stable external system already owns the capability
its security, support, and data boundaries meet the mandate
the integration can preserve auditable inputs, outputs, and authority
buildWhen: the workflow’s decision model or evidence boundary is differentiating
existing tools cannot meet the required authority, provenance, or operability
a reusable contract would reduce repeated bespoke work
validateFirst: identify the accountable human decision maker
define an acceptance evaluation and rollback path
confirm what production evidence exists versus prototype evidence

assumptions: reuse is valuable only after a real fit assessment
integration effort depends on data contracts, identity, security review, and change management
human review remains required for material decisions
nonClaims: No time, cost, adoption, reliability, or return-on-investment outcome is guaranteed.
Hapa prototype artifacts do not by themselves prove production readiness or compatibility.

authorityBoundary: Agents can retrieve, compare, propose, and prepare evidence. Humans approve scope, data access, decisions, external actions, and any production release.
claimBoundary: Professional production experience, Hapa prototypes, derived snapshots, and planning scenarios must remain separately labeled.
